Apex Hunting
Tracking and slaying a region’s apex predator is no ordinary hunt, 
and one that cannot be taken lightly. Th e apex is not a creature 
one comes across unexpected, as its presence affects large swaths 
of th region it uses as its hunting grounds and lair, and often has 
a massive influence on the natural ecology of its entire biome. 
Th ough often few in number, an apex predator is not a mythical 
beast. And their voracious appetite and size force them to distance 
themselves from each others as to not over hunt the area. It is 
only in the rare occurrences of territorial disputes or at the height 
of mating season that a Traveler could come across more than a 
singular apex predator at once, and it is highly recommended to 
put as much distance as possible between oneself and those rare 
battles or couplings, as both events can be quite cataclysmic.
Th e Travelers of Sol’Kesh are not the only ones stalking the wilds 
in search of meat and for every stalking hunter there are dozens 
of scavengers following in their wake. With the soaring skyelarx 
above, its golden eyes tracking a pursuing predator to steal from. 
Swarming scavick infest every biome that they can claw into. 
Even the deadly sacrissian, renowned for its savage predation is 
intelligent enough to know that when the scent of death is on the 
air, it can lead to an effortless meal.
Th e Scavengers Table, is not only to be used as a means of 
punishment for daring Travelers, but may also be a tool to help 
the Keeper create a living breathing world and can be used in each 
biome as a means to add a variety of beasts to every encounter. 
For in Sol'Kesh's evolutionary arms race, no meat goes wasted, 
and no step in the wilds goes unheard. 
Breath rasping between clenched teeth, blood rushing through 
veins, knuckles white with weapon gripped tight, the thrill of the 
hunt can be a savagely thrilling thing. It can also be a silent death, 
quietly stalking the tracks of beasts, pulse slowed while patiently 
waiting for the single heart-piercing strike. On the island of 
Sol’Kesh where the rule of predator and prey is law, hunting is 
often the only means to survive. Unlike the other Expeditions, 
hunting always ends in battle, but the value of their scavenged 
Components is well worth it.
Many times a Traveler will fi nd themselves requested to hunt 
and kill a specifi c creature, and tracking down a beast is more 
than simply stepping into their habitat. Gathering knowledge 
from surveying the land, conversing with those familiar with 
the animal or researching how best to make use of the intricate 
ecosystem of predators and prey, are all necessary in fi nding the 
quarry they seek. 
To go out into the wilds and hunt, a Traveler must fi rst roll on 
the biome's Hunting Expedition Table, adding any modifi ers 
that may improve their selection range. Once a prey is selected, 
either an Encounter begins immediately as the Traveler has 
successfully cornered their prey, a quest begins that may end 
with the discovery of the selected prey, or simply the prey has 
been slain and the Traveler can reap the benefi ts, it is entirely 
up to the Keeper’s discretion. A Critical failure often results in 
the Traveler and their party failing to fi nd any hint or tracks of a 
suitable beast. Although a wicked Keeper may have them instead 
get hunted in kind, perhaps by selecting a larger and more vicious 
creature that stalks the biome. 
Hunting Expedition Modifi ers
Have encountered the creature in the past • ±1 to the range result
Have gathered written or NPC given knowledge • ±1 to the range result
Have slain the biome's Apex predator in the past  • ±1 to the range result
Fully completed a Journal entry for the creature • ±2 to the range result 
Th e Primal Hunt
Voracious Scavengers Abound
When a Traveler ventures out to the untamed wilds, whether that is trudging along in the Strands' tide, or crawling through the 
Umbrawells' acid-stained tunnels that carve through the island like grubs through tree bark, there are certain survival needs that must 
always be met: warmth, shelter, clean water and food. For those living in the comfort of civilization, it is easy to forget the fortune of 
such needs being so easily satisfi ed. To those alone on a dark windswept fi eld with nothing but the stars above and the distant howls of 
predators as company, there is very little that would comfort them more than a simple tent and warm meal. 
When a Traveler prepares a meal, they must choose which ingredients (pg. 276) they would like to use from the Scavenged Components 
that they have on hand. Th ey must have access to generally clean water, an open flame, a Cooking Kit (pg. 260) or adequate cooking 
utensils. 
Example: With a thick daellash Steak Slice and a spicy Ilyrana Pepper, 
a level 8 Rogue Traveler uses these two ingredients to prepare a meal and 
must succeed on a DC 13. With a Cooking Kit on hand, they roll a Meal 
Preparation check of 11 + 3 for their Profi ciency Bonus, + 1 for having 
prepared the same meal before, and Succeed on an 15. Now with the meal 
made they can eat it and gain the added benefi ts of +1d6 Temporary Hit 
Points from the Steak Slice and Advantage on Intimidation (Charisma) 
rolls for 1 hour.
• Preparing a meal takes either 1 hour of uninterrupted time, or it 
could be performed as part of a Short or Long Rest.
• When a Traveler has all they need to begin a Meal Preparation 
roll, they must succeed on a Wisdom or Intelligence check: DC 10 
+ 3 for each ingredient added beyond the fi rst. If a nearby allied 
creature that is capable of cooking helps (an intelligent humanoid 
for an example), the Traveler can add +1 to their roll. If a Traveler 
has prepared this meal before, they can also add +1 to the result.
• When a Traveler prepares a meal, they can make enough to feed a 
number of Medium creatures equal to 1 + their Profi ciency Bonus.
A prepared meal then permanently uses up all the Scavenged 
components needed for the recipe.
• Prepared food must be eaten within 1 day of being made to gain 
the benefi ts, unless its preserved through the use of salt or cold 
temperatures. It is at the Keeper's discretion on what kinds of 
food can be preserved in this manner. A meal that is left for 3 days 
without proper preservation becomes a Poisoned Meal.
• Th ere are no restrictions to what ingredients a Traveler uses. In 
fact, it is encouraged for them to try and experiment and name 
their own recipes. Whether the Traveler knows the benefi ts of an 
ingredient is up to the Keepers discretion.
• Benefi ts from new added ingredients are accumulative. Any 
ingredients that give the same exact benefi t are not, except 
Temporary Hit Points.
• Th e lasting duration of the meal's benefi ts differ based on the 
result of the Meal Preparation roll. 
• Failing the Meal Preparation roll results in the time and 
Scavenged Components to be lost. A Critical Failure results in 
a Poisoned Meal. Any creature that consumes a Poisoned Meal 
must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution Saving Th row or take 2d6 
Poison damage.
• Rolled more than +3 the target DC: Th e benefi ts last for 2 hours
• Rolled more than +6 the target DC: Th e benefi ts last for 3 hours
• Critical Success: Th e benefi ts last for 1 day
Floating about in the Umbrawells' pitch black underwater 
rivers and lakes, the jellyfish survives with a durable 
exumbrella, covering its organs as it bumps into stone 
blindly. Long stinging tentacles trail behind it, warding 
off any predators as it filter feeds on acidophile plankton 
Clustered with its hatchling kin, the young daellash 
burrow their long bodies into the soft sand, patiently
